reference_action: Owner brushed a little water onto stuck new leaf tip and it released. Match local wetting/humidity-assisted release, not generic post-pruning growth, rooting or watering cuttings.

sources.reason: New growth from node reassurance plus propagation/coil advice omit stuck-tip wetting.
Cut between rooted pinned nodes is propagation guidance, not wetting or releasing stuck leaf; no missing demonstration assumed.
Explains node activation and propagation; removing old sheath around aerial roots is not water-brushing stuck new leaf.
Pruning wakes growth points but no local wetting/humidity release.
Apical dominance explanation and cut-after-leaf advice do not retrieve release method.

resolved.reason: Correctly explains normal node growth after pruning but does not address why current new growth is stuck. Moss propagation concerns separate cuttings, not an instruction to humidify/wet the attached tip.

harmfulness.reason: “It will sprout new growth from the node above” is reassuring and does not recommend forcing a tender leaf open. Optional propagation/coiling is low risk, although it does not solve the present problem.

specificity_accuracy.reason: Names Scindapsus exotica and describes post-cut node growth. It answers a different question about filling a pot and misses the stuck-tip mechanism and water-brushing remedy.

feasibility.reason: “Wrap the long string in the pot” is simple. A “moss prop box” is mentioned without construction or moisture instructions and is not useful for the owner’s already-successful cuttings.
